flags: Millrose completed its Spin-Off from Lennar through a distribution of approximately 80% of its Common Stock, listed its Class A common stock on the NYSE under the symbol MRP, received approximately $5.5 billion in land assets and approximately $1.0 billion in cash, and entered into a Revolving Credit Agreement up to $1.335 billion.

Millrose acquired approximately 25,000 homesites by purchasing 100% of the outstanding stock of RCH Holdings, Inc., parent holding company of Rausch, for approximately $859 million in cash net of option deposits and holdbacks.
In connection with the New Home transaction, Millrose entered into the DDTL Credit Agreement providing a delayed draw term loan facility with commitments in the aggregate amount of $1.0 billion.

flags: Sezzle submitted applications to the OCC to charter a de novo national bank, Sezzle Bank, N.A., and to the FDIC for deposit insurance, and expects to apply to the Federal Reserve to become a bank holding company.

Sezzle and WebBank entered into Second Amended Bank Program Agreements expanding their program to SezzleCash and Sezzle Send (with a $30.0 million initial loan-retention threshold, expandable to $150.0 million) and increasing Sezzle's minimum tangible net worth covenant from $12.0 million to $100.0 million.

Sezzle raised its FY2026 guidance to approximately 42.5% Total Revenue growth, $190.0 million of Adjusted Net Income (48.8% YoY growth), and $5.45–$5.50 of Adjusted Net Income per Diluted Share, and introduced preliminary FY2027 guidance of $7.20 Adjusted Net Income per Diluted Share.
TORM published its Q3 2026 results. Net profit for the quarter was USD 199m, against USD 78m in the same period of 2025.
TORM announced a dividend distribution with its Q3 2026 results. The key figures table shows a Q3 2026 dividend per share of 1.35 (USD).
In Q3 2026 TORM sold two older vessels, TORM Venture and TORM Laura. After these sales its fleet comprised 95 vessels, excluding vessels on order.

Volaris and Viva entered into a Business Combination Agreement under which Viva will merge with and into Volaris as the surviving entity, with pre-Merger Viva and Volaris shareholders holding approximately 48% and 50% of the Combined Company's capital stock (and approximately 2% held in treasury), and both companies' shareholders have approved the transaction while required regulatory approvals remain pending.

At general ordinary and general extraordinary shareholders' meetings, Volaris shareholders approved the resignation of Andrew S. Broderick from the Board of Directors, the appointment of Barron E. Steele as a proprietary director effective until the Merger Agreement with Grupo Viva Aerobús is entered into, and the ratification of Brian H. Franke as Chairman and the Board's independent members on the same conditional term.

Through its subsidiary Volaris Opco, Volaris terminated its coalition agreement for the SpinPremia loyalty program with Lealtad Mercadotecnia y Conocimientos Agregados, S.A.P.I. de C.V., a subsidiary of FEMSA.
